title: Dispatch: meaningless text now reproduces 15 of 16 facts one at a time; section vocabulary (F-018) is the one left standing
statement: On the record: 16 facts hold on the hidden pages and 2 were refuted, 71 keys have failed in every language and cipher cell tried, 51 corpora are pinned, and no anchor is confirmed. Every established fact except F-018 has been reproduced by text made without language, so the record does not yet hold a single fact that separates the manuscript from a well-tuned meaningless procedure; F-018 (the word depends on the illustration section) is the open target, though its own source warns that a table drifting along the book may pass it, which is why the attack should be tried before anyone leans on it. The literature's consecutive-line claim (Timm 2014) did not survive in our measurement: exact repetition from the line above is no larger than from four lines up (F-012 and F-015 refuted, F-017 bounds the excess at 0.025), but Timm counted similar words (one glyph apart), not identical ones, so the claim has not yet been tested on his terms, and a step to do that is coming. Next: attack F-018 first, then one generator against all 16 facts at once (G-every-fact), then a self-citation procedure with changes fixed in advance at page and section boundaries (K-003-open-1); anchor work only where a label stands beside a single drawn object, starting with the second look at N-006. Keys into the already failed language and cipher cells at the pinned budget add little and should wait for the power steps.
check: None: a dispatch. Its counts can be checked against /desk/brief and /programs/FRONTIER.md at the time of writing (2026-11-25).
